meaning_hint: Title before a married woman's surname, read 'missis'; English missis/missus is also informal for 'wife'.
examples: Mrs. Brown is our new teacher.
Good morning, Mrs. Lee!
Please give this to Mrs. Smith.
Mrs. Green lives next door.
note: Used before a married woman's last name. "Ms." is safe for any woman.

meaning_hint: In Ukrainian also a machine part or component.
examples: Send me the details.
Here are the details.
I need more details.
Check every detail.
Can I talk to the manager?
She is a manager.
The manager is not here.
My manager is nice.
She has a big role in the film.
He plays the role of a doctor.
I like his role.
This is a small role.
I live with my partner and two kids.
Find a partner and practice the dialog.
He is my business partner.
Can I bring my partner to the party?
I like your style.
This is a new style.
She has a great style.
What style do you like?

meaning_hint: The plural продукти also means groceries, food.
examples: This is a new product.
The shop has good products.
I like this product.
How much is this product?
Ha! I knew you were wrong!
Ha, that's a funny joke!
"Ha ha, very funny," she said.
Ha! I won the game again!
note: "Ha ha" shows laughing; it can also mean you are not amused.

meaning_hint: A surprise (unexpected event or gift); the feeling of surprise is здивування.
examples: We are planning a surprise party for Mom.
What a nice surprise!
I have a surprise for you.
Don't tell him, it's a surprise.

meaning_hint: Only a government minister; a church minister is священник or пастор.
examples: The minister is on TV.
She is a minister.
The minister talks to people.
Who is the new minister?
I have a meeting with a client at ten.
Our clients are very happy with our work.
She is my best client.
Please call the client back today.

meaning_hint: Soccer; American football is американський футбол.
examples: I play football.
We watch football on TV.
Football is my favorite sport.
Do you like football?
note: In the US, "football" means American football. Soccer is "soccer".

meaning_hint: A fashion model, a scale model or a version (model of a car).
examples: This is a new model.
What model is your phone?
I like this car model.
She is a fashion model.
He is a real gentleman who always opens the door.
Good evening, ladies and gentlemen.
A gentleman wants to see you at the front desk.
My grandfather was a kind old gentleman.
note: Plural: gentlemen.

meaning_hint: уїк-енд is an old dictionary spelling; the usual spelling is вікенд.
examples: What are you doing this weekend?
Have a nice weekend!
We go to the lake every weekend.
I worked all weekend.

meaning_hint: A training course or workshop; sports training is тренування.
examples: I have training today.
The training is free.
We go to a training.
The training starts at ten.
note: Training is uncountable: say "training", not "a training".

meaning_hint: The usual Ukrainian word is обід
examples: What do you want for lunch?
Let's have lunch together tomorrow.
I eat lunch at noon.
She's out for lunch right now.
note: Usually no "a": "have lunch," not "have a lunch."

meaning_hint: Only the noun; to contract (shrink) is скорочуватися.
examples: Please read the contract before you sign it.
I signed a one-year contract.
My work contract ends in May.
Can I see a copy of the contract?

meaning_hint: Usually a website; a building site is ділянка or майданчик.
examples: Visit our site.
The site is down.
I buy shoes on this site.
This site is very good.
note: Short for "website".

examples: This material is soft.
What material is this?
We need more material.
The bag is made of good material.

meaning_hint: In Ukrainian slang mostly a drug trip or a journey; neutral word for a trip: поїздка.
examples: How was your trip to the mountains?
We are going on a trip next week.
Have a good trip!
The trip to work takes one hour.
We have many activities for kids.
Swimming is a good activity.
What activities do you like?
The hotel has fun activities.

meaning_hint: Program code, PIN code, secret code; a code of law is кодекс.
examples: Enter the code to open the door.
What is the code for the Wi-Fi?
I got a code by text message.
He writes code for a big company.

meaning_hint: Also exchange rate and year of study; a meal course is страва.
examples: I'm taking an English course online.
The cooking course starts next week.
How long is the course?
She finished a computer course last year.

meaning_hint: Only a music band (also гурт); other senses of band (strip, ring) are different words.
examples: My favorite band is playing tonight.
He plays guitar in a band.
The band played for two hours.
Let's start a band!
Don't be an idiot!
I felt like an idiot at the meeting.
Some idiot parked in my space.
I'm such an idiot, I forgot my keys!
note: Rude word; be careful using it about other people.

meaning_hint: The punctuation mark (US 'period') is крапка.
examples: It is a busy period at work.
The waiting period is one week.
This is a short period of time.
I work here for a short period.

meaning_hint: A king's son; a ruling prince (e.g. of Kyivan Rus') is князь.
examples: The prince lives in a big castle.
Kids love stories about a prince and a princess.
The prince visited our city today.
The young prince got married last year.

meaning_hint: Mainly a press/TV interview; a job interview is usually співбесіда; 'to interview' = брати інтерв'ю.
examples: I have a job interview tomorrow.
How did your interview go?
I read an interview with the singer.
The interview was on TV last night.
This is my boyfriend, Tom.
She has a new boyfriend.
My boyfriend cooked dinner for me.
Do you have a boyfriend?

meaning_hint: British spelling: centre.
examples: The hotel is in the city center.
We go to the shopping center.
The center is near here.
I live in the center.
note: British spelling is "centre".

examples: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
She said goodbye and left.
We waved goodbye to our friends.
It's hard to say goodbye.
note: "Bye" is more common in casual speech.

meaning_hint: Colloquially also 'a guy, a character'.
examples: What type of music do you like?
This type of phone is very cheap.
He is not my type.
We sell all types of bread.
note: In speech, "kind" is more common: "What kind of music do you like?"

meaning_hint: Also song lyrics (текст пісні); a text message is повідомлення or SMS.
examples: Read the text and answer the questions.
The text on this sign is too small.
Please copy this text into an email.
This text is easy to understand.
note: In everyday talk, "a text" often means a phone message (SMS).

examples: Do you have internet?
The internet is slow.
I read news on the internet.
Is there internet in the hotel?
note: Say "the internet" or "on the internet".

meaning_hint: спіч = a short formal speech, often ironic; the usual word is промова; speech as an ability = мова.
examples: He gave a short speech at the wedding.
I have to make a speech tomorrow.
Her speech was very funny.
The president's speech was on TV.
You're crazy to swim in this cold water!
My kids are crazy about soccer.
Traffic was crazy this morning.
This noise is driving me crazy.
note: Informal. Can be rude when used about a person with mental illness.

examples: Let's stay in contact after the trip.
I lost contact with my old friends.
Can you send me her contact details?
Add me to your phone contacts.

meaning_hint: Also a round of a competition or election.
examples: We took a bus tour of the city.
The tour starts at ten o'clock.
Is lunch included in the tour?
The band is on tour this summer.

meaning_hint: Standard Ukrainian is коментар; комент is informal (internet).
examples: Leave a comment, please.
I read the comments.
Thanks for your comment.
This comment is funny.
He is my favorite actor.
The actor was very good in that film.
She wants to be an actor.
Many famous actors live in this city.
I watched the first episode last night.
The new episode comes out on Friday.
Each episode is about forty minutes long.
Don't tell me what happens in this episode!
Please sign this document.
Bring your documents to the office.
I need to print a document.
Save the document on your computer.
Ask an expert before you buy a car.
She is an expert in computers.
I'm not an expert, but it looks fine.
Experts say we should drink more water.
This method is easy.
I use a new method.
What method do you use?
It is a good method.

meaning_hint: A British lord (title); the Lord (God) is Господь.
examples: He became a lord last year.
The lord lived in a big castle.
The lords met to talk about the law.
My grandfather worked for a rich lord.
note: Mostly used for British nobles. With a capital L, it can also mean God.

examples: The lieutenant gave orders to the soldiers.
He was promoted to lieutenant last year.
The lieutenant led his men across the river.
Ask the lieutenant for permission.
note: Pronounced "loo-TEN-ant" in American English.

meaning_hint: A round in boxing, a game or talks; the shape 'round' is круглий.
examples: He won the fight in the third round.
Our team lost in the first round.
We played another round of cards.
The next round starts in five minutes.

meaning_hint: Only a brand (of a product); a burn mark on cattle = тавро.
examples: What brand is your phone?
This brand of coffee is very good.
I always buy the same brand of shoes.
Cheap brands are often just as good.
My little girl is an angel.
There is an angel on top of our tree.
You're an angel, thank you!
The picture shows an angel with white wings.

meaning_hint: Also a university teaching assistant; a shop assistant is продавець.
examples: Ask my assistant to call you back.
She works as a teaching assistant.
The shop assistant helped me find a size.
My assistant will send you the documents.
We swam in the ocean every day.
The hotel has a view of the ocean.
The ocean is very cold today.
I love the sound of the ocean.

meaning_hint: Formal or clinical; the everyday word is самогубство
examples: Suicide is a serious problem among young people.
If you think about suicide, call a helpline.
The film talks about suicide.
Schools teach students about suicide prevention.

meaning_hint: детектив also means a detective story or film; in English say a detective story
examples: The detective asked many questions.
She hired a private detective.
The detective found the missing ring.
I love reading detective stories.
note: In Ukrainian "детектив" can also mean a crime novel; in English say "detective story".

meaning_hint: Only the unit of length (about 30 cm; plural feet); the body part is стопа or нога.
examples: He is six feet tall.
The room is twelve feet long.
The wall is ten feet high.
This box is one foot wide.
note: Irregular plural: one foot, two feet.

examples: Hmm, I'm not sure about that.
Hmm, let me think for a minute.
Hmm, that sounds strange.
"Hmm," he said, looking at the map.
note: Informal; used in speech or texts.

meaning_hint: Also the music genre (метал).
examples: This chair is made of metal.
Metal gets hot in the sun.
Don't put metal in the microwave.
Gold is an expensive metal.
Yo, what's up?
Yo, come over here!
He said "yo" when he walked in.
Yo, can you pass me the ball?
note: Very informal slang greeting; avoid in formal situations.
